front_blocks.md: Define **database**.

back_blocks.md: A database is a **structured, persistent collection of data** that allows easy **storage, retrieval and management** of information.

cards.front_md: Define **database**.
cards.back_md: A database is a **structured, persistent collection of data** that allows easy **storage, retrieval and management** of information.

front_blocks.md: Give two benefits of an electronic database.

back_blocks.md: It is **easier to add, delete, modify and update data**, data can be **backed up and copied more easily**, and **multiple users from multiple locations** can access it at the same time.

cards.front_md: Give two benefits of an electronic database.
cards.back_md: It is **easier to add, delete, modify and update data**, data can be **backed up and copied more easily**, and **multiple users from multiple locations** can access it at the same time.

front_blocks.md: Name the two main types of database.

back_blocks.md: The two main types are **flat file** and **relational**.

cards.front_md: Name the two main types of database.
cards.back_md: The two main types are **flat file** and **relational**.

front_blocks.md: Define **flat file database**.

back_blocks.md: A flat file database stores **all data in a single table**.

cards.front_md: Define **flat file database**.
cards.back_md: A flat file database stores **all data in a single table**.

front_blocks.md: Give two drawbacks of a flat file database.

back_blocks.md: A flat file causes **data redundancy**, uses **inefficient storage**, is **harder to maintain**, and risks **inconsistent data** if a repeated value is not changed everywhere.

cards.front_md: Give two drawbacks of a flat file database.
cards.back_md: A flat file causes **data redundancy**, uses **inefficient storage**, is **harder to maintain**, and risks **inconsistent data** if a repeated value is not changed everywhere.

front_blocks.md: Define **relational database**.

back_blocks.md: A relational database organises data into **multiple tables** and uses **keys to connect related data**.

cards.front_md: Define **relational database**.
cards.back_md: A relational database organises data into **multiple tables** and uses **keys to connect related data**.

front_blocks.md: Give two benefits of a relational database.

back_blocks.md: A relational database **reduces data redundancy**, makes **efficient use of storage** and is **easier to maintain**.

cards.front_md: Give two benefits of a relational database.
cards.back_md: A relational database **reduces data redundancy**, makes **efficient use of storage** and is **easier to maintain**.

front_blocks.md: How does a relational database avoid inconsistent data?

back_blocks.md: Each piece of data is stored **only once**, so changing one piece of data updates it in the **entire database**.

cards.front_md: How does a relational database avoid inconsistent data?
cards.back_md: Each piece of data is stored **only once**, so changing one piece of data updates it in the **entire database**.

front_blocks.md: **True or False?**
A flat file database stores data in multiple linked tables.

back_blocks.md: **False.**
A **flat file** database stores all data in a **single table**. It is a **relational** database that uses multiple linked tables.

cards.front_md:
**True or False?**

A flat file database stores data in multiple linked tables.
cards.back_md:
**False.**

A **flat file** database stores all data in a **single table**. It is a **relational** database that uses multiple linked tables.

front_blocks.md: Define **table** in a database.

back_blocks.md: A table is a **complete set of records about the same subject or topic** in a database.

cards.front_md: Define **table** in a database.
cards.back_md: A table is a **complete set of records about the same subject or topic** in a database.

front_blocks.md: Define **record**.

back_blocks.md: A record is a **complete set of fields on a single entity** in a table, shown as a **row**.

cards.front_md: Define **record**.
cards.back_md: A record is a **complete set of fields on a single entity** in a table, shown as a **row**.

front_blocks.md: Why is repeating a tutor's name in every student row a problem?

back_blocks.md: It creates **redundant data**. If the tutor's name changed, **every instance** would need editing, and missing one would leave the table with **inconsistent data**.

cards.front_md: Why is repeating a tutor's name in every student row a problem?
cards.back_md: It creates **redundant data**. If the tutor's name changed, **every instance** would need editing, and missing one would leave the table with **inconsistent data**.

front_blocks.md: Define **field**.

back_blocks.md: A field is a **single piece of data in a table**, shown as a **column**.

cards.front_md: Define **field**.
cards.back_md: A field is a **single piece of data in a table**, shown as a **column**.

front_blocks.md: What is the difference between a field and a record?

back_blocks.md: A **field** is a single piece of data, shown as a **column**, while a **record** is a **group of related fields** representing one data entry, shown as a **row**.

cards.front_md: What is the difference between a field and a record?
cards.back_md: A **field** is a single piece of data, shown as a **column**, while a **record** is a **group of related fields** representing one data entry, shown as a **row**.

front_blocks.md: Define **data type**.

back_blocks.md: A data type is the **type of data that can be held in a field**, and is defined when designing a table.

cards.front_md: Define **data type**.
cards.back_md: A data type is the **type of data that can be held in a field**, and is defined when designing a table.

front_blocks.md: Name four common data types.

back_blocks.md: Common data types are **numeric** (whole or decimal), **character/string** for text data, **date/time**, and **Boolean** for true or false values.

cards.front_md: Name four common data types.
cards.back_md: Common data types are **numeric** (whole or decimal), **character/string** for text data, **date/time**, and **Boolean** for true or false values.

front_blocks.md: Which data type would be used for the price of a car?

back_blocks.md: The **numeric** data type would be used for a price.

cards.front_md: Which data type would be used for the price of a car?
cards.back_md: The **numeric** data type would be used for a price.

front_blocks.md: **True or False?**
A Boolean field stores true or false values.

back_blocks.md: **True.**
The **Boolean** data type stores **true or false** values.

cards.front_md:
**True or False?**

A Boolean field stores true or false values.
cards.back_md:
**True.**

The **Boolean** data type stores **true or false** values.

front_blocks.md: Define **primary key**.

back_blocks.md: A primary key is a **unique field that can be used to identify a record in a table**.

cards.front_md: Define **primary key**.
cards.back_md: A primary key is a **unique field that can be used to identify a record in a table**.

front_blocks.md: Define **foreign key**.

back_blocks.md: A foreign key is a **field in a table that refers to the primary key in another table**.

cards.front_md: Define **foreign key**.
cards.back_md: A foreign key is a **field in a table that refers to the primary key in another table**.

front_blocks.md: What is a foreign key used for?

back_blocks.md: A foreign key is used to **link tables** and **create relationships** between them.

cards.front_md: What is a foreign key used for?
cards.back_md: A foreign key is used to **link tables** and **create relationships** between them.

front_blocks.md: **True or False?**
The same primary key value can appear on more than one record in a table.

back_blocks.md: **False.**
A primary key is a **unique** field, so each record has its **own** primary key value.

cards.front_md:
**True or False?**

The same primary key value can appear on more than one record in a table.
cards.back_md:
**False.**

A primary key is a **unique** field, so each record has its **own** primary key value.

front_blocks.md: An orders table contains a customer_id field. Which type of key is it?

back_blocks.md: It is a **foreign key**, because it refers to the **primary key** in the customers table and links an order back to the customer who made it.

cards.front_md: An orders table contains a customer_id field. Which type of key is it?
cards.back_md: It is a **foreign key**, because it refers to the **primary key** in the customers table and links an order back to the customer who made it.

front_blocks.md: State one benefit of using a relational database.

back_blocks.md: A relational database **reduces data redundancy** and **reduces data inconsistency**.

cards.front_md: State one benefit of using a relational database.
cards.back_md: A relational database **reduces data redundancy** and **reduces data inconsistency**.

front_blocks.md: What two things can be used to perform calculations in a database?

back_blocks.md: Calculations use **arithmetic operations** or **numeric functions**.

cards.front_md: What two things can be used to perform calculations in a database?
cards.back_md: Calculations use **arithmetic operations** or **numeric functions**.

front_blocks.md: Define **calculated field**.

back_blocks.md: A calculated field is a field that **carries out a calculation based on other number fields** in the database.

cards.front_md: Define **calculated field**.
cards.back_md: A calculated field is a field that **carries out a calculation based on other number fields** in the database.

front_blocks.md: Give an example of a calculated field.

back_blocks.md: A `stockvalue` field could calculate `unit_price` multiplied by `stock`, which **multiplies the price of each item by its quantity** to find the **total value of the stock**.

cards.front_md: Give an example of a calculated field.
cards.back_md: A `stockvalue` field could calculate `unit_price` multiplied by `stock`, which **multiplies the price of each item by its quantity** to find the **total value of the stock**.

front_blocks.md: Define **calculated control**.

back_blocks.md: A calculated control is an **object placed on a form or report** to display the **result of an expression**.

cards.front_md: Define **calculated control**.
cards.back_md: A calculated control is an **object placed on a form or report** to display the **result of an expression**.

front_blocks.md: What happens to the result shown by a calculated control?

back_blocks.md: The result is **displayed on the form** but is **not stored in the database**.

cards.front_md: What happens to the result shown by a calculated control?
cards.back_md: The result is **displayed on the form** but is **not stored in the database**.

front_blocks.md: Name the four basic arithmetic operations available in a database.

back_blocks.md: The four operations are **addition**, **subtraction**, **multiplication** and **division**.

cards.front_md: Name the four basic arithmetic operations available in a database.
cards.back_md: The four operations are **addition**, **subtraction**, **multiplication** and **division**.

front_blocks.md: **True or False?**
`FinalCost = TotalCost - Discount` is an example of a subtraction operation.

back_blocks.md: **True.**
Subtracting a discount field from the total cost is a **subtraction** operation performed at run time.

cards.front_md:
**True or False?**

`FinalCost = TotalCost - Discount` is an example of a subtraction operation.
cards.back_md:
**True.**

Subtracting a discount field from the total cost is a **subtraction** operation performed at run time.

front_blocks.md: What are aggregate functions used for?

back_blocks.md: Aggregate functions **calculate statistical information about a set of records**.

cards.front_md: What are aggregate functions used for?
cards.back_md: Aggregate functions **calculate statistical information about a set of records**.

front_blocks.md: Name the five aggregate functions.

back_blocks.md: The five aggregate functions are **SUM**, **AVERAGE**, **MAX**, **MIN** and **COUNT**.

cards.front_md: Name the five aggregate functions.
cards.back_md: The five aggregate functions are **SUM**, **AVERAGE**, **MAX**, **MIN** and **COUNT**.

front_blocks.md: Which aggregate function finds the highest number in a column?

back_blocks.md: **MAX** finds the highest number in a column, and **MIN** finds the lowest.

cards.front_md: Which aggregate function finds the highest number in a column?
cards.back_md: **MAX** finds the highest number in a column, and **MIN** finds the lowest.

front_blocks.md: Define **sorting**.

back_blocks.md: Sorting is a database function that helps **organise and present data in a meaningful way**.

cards.front_md: Define **sorting**.
cards.back_md: Sorting is a database function that helps **organise and present data in a meaningful way**.

front_blocks.md: What is the difference between ascending and descending order?

back_blocks.md: **Ascending** sorts data from **smallest to largest**, such as A to Z or 1 to 100. **Descending** sorts from **largest to smallest**, such as Z to A or 100 to 1.

cards.front_md: What is the difference between ascending and descending order?
cards.back_md: **Ascending** sorts data from **smallest to largest**, such as A to Z or 1 to 100. **Descending** sorts from **largest to smallest**, such as Z to A or 100 to 1.

front_blocks.md: Give an example of sorting on a single criterion.

back_blocks.md: Sorting a list of customers into **ascending order by their last names** uses a single criterion.

cards.front_md: Give an example of sorting on a single criterion.
cards.back_md: Sorting a list of customers into **ascending order by their last names** uses a single criterion.

back_blocks.md: Sorting customers **first by last name** in ascending order, and then **by city** in descending order within each last name, uses multiple criteria.

cards.back_md: Sorting customers **first by last name** in ascending order, and then **by city** in descending order within each last name, uses multiple criteria.

cards.front_md: Define **searching**.

**True or False?**

A query can only be based on a single criterion.

front_blocks.md: What is the difference between the AND and OR operators?

back_blocks.md: **AND** returns true if **both conditions are met**, while **OR** returns true if **at least one condition is met**.

cards.front_md: What is the difference between the AND and OR operators?
cards.back_md: **AND** returns true if **both conditions are met**, while **OR** returns true if **at least one condition is met**.

front_blocks.md: What does the NOT operator return?

back_blocks.md: **NOT** returns true if the condition is **not met**.

cards.front_md: What does the NOT operator return?
cards.back_md: **NOT** returns true if the condition is **not met**.

front_blocks.md: What is the LIKE operator used for?

back_blocks.md: **LIKE** returns true if the value **matches a pattern**, and is used with **wildcards**.

cards.front_md: What is the LIKE operator used for?
cards.back_md: **LIKE** returns true if the value **matches a pattern**, and is used with **wildcards**.

front_blocks.md: Name three comparison operators.

back_blocks.md: The comparison operators are **>**, **<**, **=**, **>=**, **<=** and **<>**.

cards.front_md: Name three comparison operators.
cards.back_md: The comparison operators are **>**, **<**, **=**, **>=**, **<=** and **<>**.

front_blocks.md: What do the wildcard characters %, _ and * represent?

back_blocks.md: **%** represents **zero, one or multiple characters**, **_** represents a **single character**, and **\*** represents **all**.

front_blocks.md: Define **database form**.

back_blocks.md: A form is a tool used to **capture data to be stored in a database**.

cards.front_md: Define **database form**.
cards.back_md: A form is a tool used to **capture data to be stored in a database**.

front_blocks.md: Give two examples of a form.

back_blocks.md: An **online form to sign up to a website**, and **filling in personal details on a mobile device to join a gym**.

cards.front_md: Give two examples of a form.
cards.back_md: An **online form to sign up to a website**, and **filling in personal details on a mobile device to join a gym**.

front_blocks.md: Name the five characteristics of good form design.

back_blocks.md: Good form design has **simplicity**, **ease of use**, an **intuitive layout**, **clear labels** and **appropriate controls**.

cards.front_md: Name the five characteristics of good form design.
cards.back_md: Good form design has **simplicity**, **ease of use**, an **intuitive layout**, **clear labels** and **appropriate controls**.

front_blocks.md: What does an intuitive layout mean on a form?

back_blocks.md: **Related fields are grouped together** and the **sequence of fields follows a logical order**.

cards.front_md: What does an intuitive layout mean on a form?
cards.back_md: **Related fields are grouped together** and the **sequence of fields follows a logical order**.

front_blocks.md: Why should each field on a form have a clear label?

back_blocks.md: A clear, concise label **indicates what information is expected** in that field.

cards.front_md: Why should each field on a form have a clear label?
cards.back_md: A clear, concise label **indicates what information is expected** in that field.

front_blocks.md: Name three control elements used on a form.

back_blocks.md: Controls include **radio buttons**, **check boxes**, **drop-down menus**, a **submit button**, a **save button**, and **next and previous record buttons**.

cards.front_md: Name three control elements used on a form.
cards.back_md: Controls include **radio buttons**, **check boxes**, **drop-down menus**, a **submit button**, a **save button**, and **next and previous record buttons**.

front_blocks.md: When are radio buttons used?

back_blocks.md: Radio buttons are used when there is a list of **two or more options that are mutually exclusive**.

cards.front_md: When are radio buttons used?
cards.back_md: Radio buttons are used when there is a list of **two or more options that are mutually exclusive**.

front_blocks.md: When are check boxes used?

back_blocks.md: Check boxes are used when the user can **select multiple options from a list**.

cards.front_md: When are check boxes used?
cards.back_md: Check boxes are used when the user can **select multiple options from a list**.

front_blocks.md: When are drop-down menus used?

back_blocks.md: Drop-down menus are used when you want to provide **many options but conserve space**.

cards.front_md: When are drop-down menus used?
cards.back_md: Drop-down menus are used when you want to provide **many options but conserve space**.

front_blocks.md: **True or False?**
Check boxes should be used when the options are mutually exclusive.

back_blocks.md: **False.**
**Radio buttons** are used for mutually exclusive options. **Check boxes** are used when the user can select **multiple** options.

cards.front_md:
**True or False?**

Check boxes should be used when the options are mutually exclusive.
cards.back_md:
**False.**

**Radio buttons** are used for mutually exclusive options. **Check boxes** are used when the user can select **multiple** options.

back_blocks.md: White space **improves readability** and **reduces cognitive load**.

cards.front_md: Why is white space important on a form?
cards.back_md: White space **improves readability** and **reduces cognitive load**.
